opening.text: Most families have a box. It might be a shoebox, a drawer or a folder on a phone. Inside are old photos of people we never met. Some faces look a little like ours. Each one lived a whole life. Family history is opening that box and asking, "Who were you?"

mainMessage.text: Family history is about people. Every one of them has a story, and we can help it be remembered.

blocks.text: **Every life has a story** The Lord keeps a record of people who think of Him. Every life is written down somewhere in heaven.

Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “We Each Have a Story” from the April 2022 general conference.
We each have a story.
Your story matters, and so does theirs.
**Say the names** Helaman gave his sons the names of their ancestors. He knew that remembering a name helps us remember a life.

Behold, my sons, I desire that ye should remember to keep the commandments of God; and I would that ye should declare unto the people these words. Behold, I have given unto you the names of our first parents who came out of the land of Jerusalem; and this I have done that when you remember your names ye may remember them; and when ye remember them ye may remember their works; and when ye remember their works ye may know how that it is said, and also written, that they were good. Therefore, my sons, I would that ye should do that which is good, that it may be said of you, and also written, even as it has been said and written of them.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “We Each Have a Story” from the April 2022 general conference.
Still very much alive, our ancestors deserve to be remembered.
A name remembered is a life honored.
**Two doors, one house** Family history and temple work may seem like different things. They are one work. We find the names, and the temple gives them blessings.

And now, my dearly beloved brethren and sisters, let me assure you that these are principles in relation to the dead and the living that cannot be lightly passed over, as pertaining to our salvation. For their salvation is necessary and essential to our salvation, as Paul says concerning the fathers—that they without us cannot be made perfect—neither can we without our dead be made perfect.
Elder Benjamín De Hoyos of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Work of the Temple and Family History—One and the Same Work” from the April 2023 general conference.
Certainly, the work of the temple and family history are one and the same work in the Church.
The box and the temple belong together.
**You are not alone in this** Some people feel they are not good at this. The Lord says He will help.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Elder Benjamín De Hoyos of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Work of the Temple and Family History—One and the Same Work” from the April 2023 general conference.
To those of you who do not feel capable of doing this work, you should know that you are not alone.
Help is closer than you think.
**Home in families** The purpose is a family together. God wants His children home again.

Brethren, shall we not go on in so great a cause? Go forward and not backward. Courage, brethren; and on, on to the victory! Let your hearts rejoice, and be exceedingly glad. Let the earth break forth into singing. Let the dead speak forth anthems of eternal praise to the King Immanuel, who hath ordained, before the world was, that which would enable us to redeem them out of their prison; for the prisoners shall go free.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Gathering the Family of God” from the April 2017 general conference.
God the Father wants His children home again, in families and in glory.
The goal is everyone home.
**Ask the elders** Moses told Israel to ask their fathers and elders about the days of old. Older relatives hold stories we can still gather.
Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “We Each Have a Story” from the April 2022 general conference.
Please come find your family, all your generations, and bring them home.
Ask while you still can.

story.title: Stones of remembrance

blocks.text: When Israel crossed the Jordan, Joshua had them set up stones. The stones were there so that children would ask questions.

That this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean ye by these stones? Then ye shall answer them, That the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the Lord; when it passed over Jordan, the waters of Jordan were cut off: and these stones shall be for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever.
Stories need someone to ask and someone to answer. Family history works the same way.

application.text: First, pick one older relative. Second, ask them one question about their life. Third, write down what they say.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that families are meant to be together. I know our ancestors are not forgotten by God. I know that Jesus Christ makes it possible for families to be joined forever. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Look at an old tree. What you see is the trunk and the branches. But most of the tree is underground. The roots go deep. They hold it up and feed it. We are like that tree. Our ancestors are our roots. They are out of sight, but they hold us up.

mainMessage.text: Family history is learning about our roots. When we do, we stand taller and feel more at home.

blocks.text: **Every root has a story** The Lord keeps a book of remembrance. Every person in our family tree is written there.

Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “We Each Have a Story” from the April 2022 general conference.
We each have a story.
Every root has a story.

Behold, my sons, I desire that ye should remember to keep the commandments of God; and I would that ye should declare unto the people these words. Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “We Each Have a Story” from the April 2022 general conference.
Still very much alive, our ancestors deserve to be remembered.
The roots are still alive.
**Roots and branches grow together** A tree can't live with only roots or only branches. We need our ancestors, and they need us.

And now, my dearly beloved brethren and sisters, let me assure you that these are principles in relation to the dead and the living that cannot be lightly passed over, as pertaining to our salvation. For their salvation is necessary and essential to our salvation, as Paul says concerning the fathers—that they without us cannot be made perfect—neither can we without our dead be made perfect.
Elder Benjamín De Hoyos of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Work of the Temple and Family History—One and the Same Work” from the April 2023 general conference.
Certainly, the work of the temple and family history are one and the same work in the Church.
Tree and roots are one living thing.
**Water and sun** A tree needs help to grow. The Lord promises to help us in this work. We won't be left on our own.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Elder Benjamín De Hoyos of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Work of the Temple and Family History—One and the Same Work” from the April 2023 general conference.
To those of you who do not feel capable of doing this work, you should know that you are not alone.
Growth comes with help.
**A tree for the whole family** A family tree is a family together. God wants His children home again.

Brethren, shall we not go on in so great a cause? Go forward and not backward. Courage, brethren; and on, on to the victory! Let your hearts rejoice, and be exceedingly glad. Let the earth break forth into singing. Let the dead speak forth anthems of eternal praise to the King Immanuel, who hath ordained, before the world was, that which would enable us to redeem them out of their prison; for the prisoners shall go free.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Gathering the Family of God” from the April 2017 general conference.
God the Father wants His children home again, in families and in glory.
The whole tree is meant to be together.
**Dig a little** To see roots, you have to dig. We can ask our elders and look in records.
Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “We Each Have a Story” from the April 2022 general conference.
Please come find your family, all your generations, and bring them home.
Start digging gently.

story.title: Tell your children

blocks.text: God told Israel to teach their children what He had done. The children would ask, and the parents would answer.

And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say unto you, What mean ye by this service? That ye shall say, It is the sacrifice of the Lord’s passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses. And the people bowed the head and worshipped.
Roots are passed on by telling. Each generation hands the story to the next.

application.text: First, draw a simple tree with your name at the bottom. Second, add your parents and grandparents. Third, mark one name you want to learn more about.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I am grateful for those who came before me. I know they are part of my story. I know God keeps the family tree together. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

mainMessage.text: Every family has missing pieces. When we find them, the picture is more whole and more beautiful.

blocks.text: **Each piece has a picture on it** Every piece is part of the larger picture. Every person in our family has a story that belongs.

Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.

story.title: Teach them diligently

blocks.text: Moses told Israel to put God's words in their hearts. Then they were to teach them to their children, day in and day out.

And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
Pieces are handed down in daily talk. Ordinary moments carry family stories.

application.text: First, find one thing you don't know about your family's past. Second, ask someone who might know. Third, record the answer in a notebook or on your phone.

mainMessage.text: We are a link in a long chain of hands. Family history is how we thank those who carried the light before us and prepare to hand it on.

blocks.text: **The light has a story** Each hand that held the lantern has a story. Each of our ancestors lived, worked and hoped.

story.title: Why the records were kept

blocks.text: Alma told his son Helaman why the old records had been kept. They were kept to help people remember.

And now, it has hitherto been wisdom in God that these things should be preserved; for behold, they have enlarged the memory of this people, yea, and convinced many of the error of their ways, and brought them to the knowledge of their God unto the salvation of their souls.
Records carry the light across the years. What is written down can reach those who come after.

application.text: First, think of who handed you the light in your family. Second, write them a short note of thanks, or write one in your journal. Third, plan one story you will pass on.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I am thankful for those who carried the light before me. I know it will not go out. I know Jesus Christ is the Light of the World. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

mainMessage.text: Family history is a key. It opens the way to know our ancestors, to bless them and to feel the Lord's love for our whole family.

blocks.text: **A key worth keeping** The Lord keeps a record of people who honor Him. Every one of them is worth remembering.

Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name.

**You don't have to turn it alone** If the lock is stiff, don't give up. The Lord says He will strengthen and help you.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they found a record or a story about an ancestor that surprised them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi's family gets the records

blocks.text: Nephi and his brothers brought the records back from Jerusalem. They searched them and found them precious.

And we had obtained the records which the Lord had commanded us, and searched them and found that they were desirable; yea, even of great worth unto us, insomuch that we could preserve the commandments of the Lord unto our children.
The records were worth the trouble. They helped a family remember who they were. Records still do that for us.

application.text: First, find one record about an ancestor, such as a photo, a letter or a certificate. Second, learn one fact about them you did not know. Third, share it with someone in your family.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Lord opens doors for those who seek. I know that families are meant to be together. I know Jesus Christ holds the keys of life. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
